findings.title: Accidental gitlink/submodule added to repository
findings.body: The PR adds a file named `sentry-repo` containing `Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a`, but there is no `.gitmodules` entry or submodule metadata. This is an accidental repository artifact: checkouts and CI tooling can treat it as an uninitialized submodule, create an empty directory, or fail submodule validation. Remove this file from the PR.

findings.title: Upsampling check uses the wrong dataset in split-query paths
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives a `scoped_dataset` argument, but the new upsampling eligibility call passes the closed-over `dataset` from `get_event_stats_factory`. In dashboard-widget split paths, `_get_event_stats` is called with `discover` or another dataset while the closure still holds the original dataset. `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` then evaluates the wrong dataset, so error queries split to `discover` from a metrics dataset are not upsampled. The inverse could also transform columns using a dataset that `scoped_dataset` does not support. Pass `scoped_dataset` to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`.

findings.title: Substring check misclassifies negated and mixed queries as error-only
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` treats any query containing the literal text `event.type:error` as an error-only query. This incorrectly classifies negated queries such as `!event.type:error`, mixed queries such as `event.type:transaction OR event.type:error`, and even string literals containing that text. For the `discover` dataset the endpoint then rewrites `count()` to `upsampled_count()` = `sum(sample_weight)`, so transaction or mixed rows are aggregated with a column that does not apply to them. That can produce undercounted or otherwise incorrect results. Parse the search query or require an exact, non-negated event-type term before enabling upsampling.

findings.title: Top-events ranking still uses raw count after count() is upsampled
findings.body: Only `final_columns` is transformed for upsampling. The top-events call still passes `orderby=self.get_orderby(request)` unchanged (also at line 241 for the RPC path). If a top-events request orders by `count()`, groups are selected using raw event count while the returned time series uses `upsampled_count()`. Groups with different sample weights can therefore be ranked incorrectly, and the returned top-N groups can disagree with their displayed upsampled counts. Transform count() in the orderby expressions too, or make the orderby use the upsample-aware alias.
